subject: BlueHarbor regional switchover playbook — Q&A and evidence request
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@blueharbor.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@blueharbor.com, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@blueharbor.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: BlueHarbor - regional switchover playbook Q&A

Hi Priya / Aditya,

Thanks for sending the initial playbook draft. Our ops and resiliency team reviewed and had a few high-level asks before we include Redwood in our runbook:

1) Please confirm RTO and RPO commitments for the hosted Redwood API vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity). Concrete numbers for the following scenarios would be ideal:
   - Regional outage (primary AZ/region down, failover to secondary region)
   - Zone outage with partial instance loss
   - Full failover during an ongoing long-running streaming session

2) We need a short sequence of steps (operator-run) for the suggested switchover that includes: DNS cutover approach and expected DNS TTL considerations, model certificate handling, KV cache warm-up guidance, and how to validate no-data-loss for customer tokens/usage logs.

3) Can you attach any evidence or past runbook excerpts (sanitized) where a multi-region switchover was executed? A short matrix showing expected recovery timelines (best/typical/worst) across components (API frontends, model replicas, logs/usage, billing records) would help.

We'd appreciate a response by EOD Wednesday (PST) — our DR tabletop is next week.

Best,
Samantha Liu
Senior Ops Manager, Resiliency
BlueHarbor Financial

[Attachment: blueharbor-playbook-asklist.txt (text)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-19T01:30:00Z
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor - regional switchover playbook Q&A

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a consolidated short-form playbook and an RTO/RPO matrix for the scenarios you outlined. High level answers below; engineering details and caveats from Karthik are cc'd.

- Hosted API (shared):
  - Regional outage: target RTO 30-60 minutes (typical ~35m) for full traffic restoration to a warm secondary region; RPO depends on your ingestion pattern (we provide asynchronous cross-region replication for usage/billing logs with typical lag < 5m under normal load).
  - Zone outage: failover within a region is automated across AZs; most requests see <120s disruption, and traffic ramps as instances reattach. RPO effectively zero for in-flight data at the API layer (stateless request) but for long streaming sessions, session continuity is not guaranteed.

- Dedicated (customer-owned pools):
  - Regional outage: for Dedicated customers that opt-in to cross-region model replication and standby nodes, we can commit to RTO 15-30 minutes (configurable) for model-serving endpoints; RPO 0-2 minutes for metadata and usage logs when you enable our priority replication pipeline.

- DNS and cutover: we recommend a staged DNS cutover with low TTL (60s) pre-tabletop and a CNAME-based switchover. Playbook contains the step-by-step sequence: 1) Shift read traffic to secondary, 2) validate model warm probes, 3) cut CNAME, 4) increase capacity, 5) monitor.

- KV cache warm-up: we ship a warm-up tool that replays recent request prefixes to populate KV cache; typical warm-up achieves ~70% steady-state cache hit within 10–15 minutes for conversational workloads.

Attached: switchover-playbook-v1.pdf, rto-rpo-matrix.xlsx, network-topology-diagram.png.

Next: Karthik will add the low-level technical caveats (stateful sessions, prefix cache, quantized model load times). If you want an SSO test account in the secondary region for tabletop, say the word and we’ll provision.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: BlueHarbor - regional switchover playbook Q&A

Samantha — quick engineering notes and caveats (picking up on Priya's summary):

1) Model replication and cold start:
   - For large LLM weights (100B+), loading a quantized model into GPU memory can be the dominant factor on cold start; typical load times on our optimized runtime are 90–300s depending on instance type and model format.
   - We offer pre-warmed standby replicas for Dedicated customers; these reduce effective model availability time to <30s because the model is already resident.

2) Streaming sessions and in-flight state:
   - Our platform does not persist per-token ephemeral streaming state to durable storage by default. For continuity of long-running streaming conversations we recommend a short client-side checkpointing approach (send last n tokens on reconnect) or using our optional session persistence layer (configurable, adds ~150ms write latency).

3) Data replication and RPO:
   - Usage and billing logs: asynchronous cross-region replication with typical tail latency < 300s; enabling the priority replication channel reduces that to <30s.
   - Customer-supplied data (files, embeddings): S3-backed object replication follows the storage provider's replication SLA; we integrate with your replication buckets where requested.

4) Network and DNS specifics:
   - We advise a pre-cutover DNS TTL of 60s for the plan window. If you are unable to change TTLs, we can coordinate an IP-based front-door with short-lived certificates, but that raises complexity for cert rotation.

5) Validation & runbook checks:
   - Health checks: model probe + inference sanity checks (latency and sample output), KV cache hit-rate, and a smoke billing check (ingest and retrieval of a synthetic event).

I can provide a short script to automate warm-up probes and smoke tests if that helps the tabletop.

—Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Priya / Karthik —

Thanks for the detail, that helps. A few follow-ups before our tabletop:

• For Dedicated customers opting for pre-warmed replicas, is there a recommended minimum standby capacity (number of GPUs) relative to production QPS to meet the 15–30m RTO? Any guidance / formula you use for capacity planning?

• Can Karthik share the warm-up probe script you mentioned (we prefer something we can run from our CICD during the drill)?

• We need to understand SLA credit mechanics: if the region fails and the recovery exceeds your stated RTO, what is BlueHarbor's recourse under Redwood's hosted pricing vs dedicated contract?

• Lastly, we'd like to request a sanitized debrief (postmortem) of a prior multi-region switchover event if available — even an internal sanitized timeline is useful.

Tom (cc) will be the procurement lead for this deal; he may follow up on contract language for Dedicated commitments.

Best,
Samantha

Subject: Re: BlueHarbor - regional switchover playbook Q&A

Samantha / Tom —

Appreciate the thorough review. Quick commercial / next-step notes:

1) Standby sizing: We'll share our capacity planning doc. As a rule of thumb for Dedicated we recommend standby capacity at 20–30% of peak GPU count for fast failover; exact numbers depend on model family and expected p99 latency targets. We'll include a simple calculator you can use.

2) Warm-up script & automation: Karthik will share the warm-up probe script (we'll provide it as a small repo and a pre-built task for common CI systems).

3) SLA credits: For Hosted API we provide service credits per our public SLA, which is limited for regional disaster events; for Dedicated customers we negotiate enhanced SLA terms (financial credits and defined remediation/rollback runbooks) in the contract. Tom — happy to set a short call to align on language.

4) Postmortem: We can provide a sanitized timeline and learnings from an internal multi-region failover we performed last year (redacted customer names). Expect that in a follow-up email — we'll sanitize and deliver as a short PDF.

Next steps: I'll schedule a 30-min tabletop prep session for Wednesday PST and include a small list of smoke-test scripts for your team to run. Priya / Karthik / Grace will join.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
